_about: Chapter Q (Predicates and motif) of the suite results document: the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 in R.json's format, written for the union of manifest v4 and v5 (the chapter's 32 scenarios, 6 families and 9 units are the same in both). `summary` and `coverage_gap` are printed first on the chapter page, `intro` (the shortened background) after the computed lines; `families` keys on the family id with a title, one paragraph and a `claim`; `units` on the unit id with one property line; `mcp_notes.units` holds the one line under a unit whose MCP column is wholly not exercised. Every figure of the run is a placeholder the generator fills (doc/facts.py: chapter_facts for summary / coverage_gap / intro, family_facts for a family's paragraph, unit_facts for an MCP note) and every sentence whose truth depends on the run is a conditional `[[flag ? when true | when false]]`. The literal numbers are constants of the SPEC, of the manifest (v4 and v5 share them for this chapter) and of the service, each listed under `_assumes` with its source. Every claim follows SPEC-pattern-search.md sections 19 (predicates), 20.9 (predicates on supported paths) and 25 (motif), areas.py gen_Q, checks.py and service_by_design.json. The catalogue entries of the check kinds this chapter uses are in checks.json (status, invariants, budget_respected) and checks-QCND.json (answer_fields, contains_source_context, counts_consistent, cut, entry_fields, motif, notes, path_absent, path_record_verified, predicate_either_mirror, predicate_selected, stop, withheld); the by-design cases it names are in cases-QCND.json. Readability review (READ-306 to READ-309, 2026-10-16): a `purpose` slot; the Background opens with a vocabulary bridge (a label is an index column, the filtered item a context, a selection a label-support statement, the stronger record_verified check named) and describes the motif verdict as one statement on the union with decided_by naming the evidence; Q-pred labels the human-column assumption of its negative forms and the claim carries it; Q-strands separates the match's orientation from the annotation row read; Q-motif has a toy example labelled as such; every unit carries a reader-level `question`; access path replaces arm in the prose.

title: Predicates and motif
purpose: A predicate lets a user ask /pattern not only where a short pattern occurs but under which labels: keep only the contexts (k-mers at offsets) whose annotation row carries, or lacks, the named taxid columns, and, as a motif question, whether the pattern as a whole is found under those labels anywhere. The chapter's evidence is a planted witness of I.2's second kind: windows cut from known records, whose own taxid column is known to carry them, must be selected or left out exactly as each operator says; the strand rule and the budgets are checked against the SPEC's wording. A selected context is a label-support statement about one k-mer, not a placement of a longer sequence in one record (I.1's result units); the Background says where the stronger check is made.

intro: *What a predicate selects.* A label here is an index column, on this index a taxid written as a string (`"562"`): it says that some record of that taxid carries the k-mer. The item being filtered is a context, one k-mer of the index holding the pattern at one offset and orientation (I.1), and a predicate is a question over the labels of that k-mer's row. Selecting a context under `any(A)` therefore establishes that the k-mer is carried by some record of A, and nothing about which record, where in it, or whether a longer sequence occurs there contiguously. Three counts arrive in this order: the raw count of contexts the pattern has, `counts.tested` (how many the pass read) and `counts.selected` (how many the predicate kept). The stronger claim, that a whole path longer than k is carried by one record at one place, is made only by `record_verified` support, checked in this chapter by Q-supported (under `long_search` `supported_paths`) and in chapters L and P. A predicate (SPEC-pattern-search section 19) is asked of each graph context of a pattern of at most k bases: the seven operators `any`, `all`, `none`, `at_least` (n of a list), `and`, `or` and `not` over names that are column labels as stored. The names are bound once per request; an unknown name is absent from every context and is folded away (section 19.4: `any` of unknown names is `false`, `none` of them `true`), the result being the normal form the answer echoes; a constant normal form is evaluated without reading any row (`selection.pass` `constant`, note `predicate_constant`). A context is selected when the normal form holds on its label set: the row of its k-mer and, with `predicate_strands` `either` (the default) on this basic graph, the row of its reverse complement; `context` reads the k-mer's row only. Support is strand-consistent (section 19.5): a label supports a context as a whole, from the k-mer's row or from its mirror's, and the answer states which (`selection_strands` per label). `output.labels` `predicate_only` lists the predicate's labels found on the listed contexts; the selected contexts are the entry's results, with `counts.tested` and `counts.selected` beside the raw count. The selection is budgeted (section 19.9): `max_predicate_contexts` admits a raw count up to it (above: `withheld` `predicate_above_threshold` in `all_or_count`, a cut of the raw release in `partial`), `max_predicate_work` bounds the pass's reads (a row costs at least 8 units; at the budget the pass stops with `stop` with the phase selection and the reason `max_predicate_work` and the list is withheld as `predicate_budget`). With `long_search` `supported_paths` the predicate selects among the supported paths of a pattern longer than k, decided on the labels supporting the whole walk (section 20.9). With `predicate_scope` `motif` (section 25) the predicate is also asked once of the pattern as a whole, on the union of the labels over its contexts: `motif.selected` says whether the union satisfies the normal form, one statement about the union and none about any single context, and `decided_by` names the evidence the verdict rests on (`every_context` when every raw context was tested, `no_instance` when the pattern has no context on this graph), never the quantifier of the predicate; Q-motif has the example.

Ground truth. The windows are cut from the records of I.2: a 25 bp window of a low-carrier record (buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso; tth, pfa, cal, hvo for the `either` forms) whose contexts the record's own taxid column A supports and the human column (hsa) does not; the 20 bp windows of Q-strands sit in a 16S gene of eco, sau and pae at a site whose surrounding 42 bp the record also holds reverse-complemented (rRNA operons on both strands), so that the window's `-` contexts are reverse complements of the record's own k-mers; Q-supported takes 60 bp windows of buc and sso. Every request names `time_budget_ms` [[manifest_version >= 6 ? 110,000 | 60,000]] and `max_contexts` 10,000 as the service sends them, and every request with a predicate `max_predicate_contexts` 10,000 (the three without one, Q-pred-0014, Q-motif-0004 and -0005, omit it), so that the three access paths ask the same question; the three budget scenarios lower `max_predicate_contexts` or `max_predicate_work` to 1. A 503 deadline is therefore allowed under load and reads inconclusive, a finding only when delivered more than max(1 s, the budget) after the budget (appendix A, `budget_respected`).

Via MCP a predicate request is the `pattern_search` tool, which sends the request to the host through the service's queue: a predicate the host would refuse is refused by the service at submit, in its own words (`pattern_invalid`, the field naming the path of the first fault), and a predicate option without a predicate (`predicate_strands`, `predicate_scope` motif) is refused too, where the host accepts the first as a no-op; appendix B names every case with the service's code and text. The host's 503 deadline comes back as the service's failed task (`pattern.deadline_ends_task`, a by-design pair), and the service's answer carries no `timing.elapsed_ms`, so `budget_respected` is not exposed on that access path.

Q-pred.title: predicates
Q-pred.prose: The operators on a 25 bp window of a low-carrier record, each form once under `predicate_strands` `context` (Q-pred-forms: `any(A)`, `none(A)`, `all(A, human)`, `at_least` 1 and 2 of (A, human), `and(any A, not any human)`) and the four simple forms under `either` (Q-pred-either: `any`, `none`, `not(any)`, `all` of A alone), with `output.labels` `predicate_only`. The property (`predicate_selected`) is that the record's own contexts, every (k-mer, offset) pair of the record holding the window on `+`, are selected exactly when the predicate says so: listed where the form holds (on the `context` forms with A among their `selection_labels` and a selection strand of `context` or `both`; the Q-pred-either forms and Q-pred-0012 check the selection alone), absent from a complete filtered list where it does not. *An assumption of these fixtures, not a proved fact.* The forms that must be false (`none(A)`, `all(A, human)`, `at_least` 2 of (A, human)) rest on the window's contexts carrying A and not the human column (hsa). The low-carrier choice and the DUST filter make that likely; the builder does not prove it and the run does not verify it independently: a window of a gene conserved into the human genome would carry hsa, `all(A, human)` and `at_least` 2 would then select the record's contexts, and the suite would record a failure of the fixture's expectation without any predicate-engine error. So the forms with planted positive support (`any(A)`, the single-label forms, `at_least` 1 and the A side of `and(any A, not any human)`) check the operators against a known carrier, while the negative multi-label forms check them against an assumed non-carrier; `all` of two labels on a context carrying both is tested nowhere (the coverage paragraph). Q-pred-unknown asks an unknown label (a taxid no column has): `any` of it folds to `false`, so the answer states `predicate.unknown_labels` with that name and a normal form `false`, the entry `selection.pass` `constant` with `selected` exact 0 and the note `predicate_constant` (`answer_fields`, `entry_fields`, `notes`); `none` of it folds to `true`, a normal form `true` that selects every context (section 19.4). Q-pred-refusals holds the two code-derived refusals: a number as a name (400 `invalid_request` with the fix, write a taxid as `"562"`) and `predicate_only` without a predicate (400, the text naming `request.predicate`). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[n_mcp_by_design ? Via MCP the {n_mcp_by_design:word} refusal{n_mcp_by_design:s} stand{n_mcp_by_design:v} by design: the service's own validation refuses at submit ({mcp_refused_before_host_codes}; see B)[[!mcp_by_design_all_verified ?, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified} pair{n_mcp_by_design_unverified:s} unverified]].]]
Q-pred.claim: the seven operators select the record's contexts as SPEC-pattern-search section 19.3 reads them (the multi-label forms that must be false rest on the fixtures' unproved assumption that the human column lacks the window), an unknown name folds away before any row is read, and a malformed predicate is refused with the host's text

Q-strands.title: both strands
Q-strands.prose: Two axes are in play and must be kept apart. The first is the orientation of the match: a `+` context holds the pattern as written, a `-` context holds its reverse complement; this says how the pattern sits in the k-mer and nothing about which strand of any genome the sequence was observed on. The second is which annotation row may support the context: `predicate_strands` `context` reads only the row of the k-mer as deposited, `either` (the default) reads that row and the row of the k-mer's reverse complement, and the answer's `selection_strands` names, per label, the row that supported the decision (`context`, `reverse_complement` or `both`): the evidence source, not a count of observations. So a `-` result can be selected with `selection_strands` `context`, when the deposited k-mer's own row carries the label, and `either` alone never establishes two independent strand observations; it only widens which row may be read. The fixture supplies both orientations on purpose: a 20-mer downstream of the `515F` site in a 16S gene of eco, sau and pae, chosen so that the 42 bp around it (the window with k - 20 bases on each side, every k-mer holding the window) also occurs reverse-complemented in the record, under `any(A)` with `predicate_strands` `either`. Two properties: the `+` contexts, the record's own k-mers, are selected by their own row (`predicate_selected` with a selection strand of `context` or `both`), and at least one returned `-` context whose reverse complement is a record k-mer is selected by A through its mirror, with the selection strand `reverse_complement` or `both` (`predicate_either_mirror`, SPEC-pattern-search section 19.5). The second is the claim that `either` reads the mirror's row; the builder guarantees the mirrors exist (a mirror check with no mirror would test nothing), and the check reads only mirrors the record holds, so other records' rows cannot satisfy it. The manifest classes these tests slow. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}[[n_time_limited ?; a selection the time budget cut hides the mirrors, so the claim reads inconclusive there ({time_limited_text})]]. | In this run every test passed on every access path.]]
Q-strands.claim: under predicate_strands either a label selects a context through the row of its reverse complement, and the answer says so

Q-more.title: more predicates
Q-more.prose: Three further forms on 25 bp windows: the reverse complement of a mja window under `context` strands, whose source contexts are `-` contexts selected by their own rows (`predicate_selected` on strand `-` with the selection strand `context`: a `-` context's own row is the row of the k-mer as deposited, the record's: the orientation axis of Q-strands' explanation, read under `context` strands); `or(any human, any A)` under `either` on tth, selected; and `at_least` 3 of two labels, refused with 400 `invalid_request` naming `request.predicate.at_least.n` (section 19.3: n is an integer from 1 to the list's length). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[x[Q-more-0003][mcp][standing] = by design ? Via MCP the refusal is the service's own at submit (`pattern.predicate_form_other`, see B).]]
Q-more.claim: a '-' context is selected on its own row under context strands, or() selects, and n outside 1 .. the list's length is refused

Q-supported.title: supported paths
Q-supported.prose: A 60 bp window of buc and of sso searched as supported paths (`long_search` `supported_paths`, `max_paths` 1,024, `output.labels` `predicate_only`) under two predicates: `none(A)` in `partial` with `context` strands, where the record's own path must not be among the results (`path_absent`: no listed path spells the window; a cut or withheld list that can have happened makes it inconclusive, nothing else is assumed of the other paths), and `any(A)` under `either` in `all_or_count`, where the record's path is listed with the record's taxid at support `record_verified` and an occurrence at the window's coordinates and strand (`path_record_verified`). Under `either` the decision needs the mirror's support, so the supported walks are held and decided after the search (section 20.9); the pair shows both directions of the selection on the same window. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path.]]
Q-supported.claim: a predicate selects among supported paths: none(A) leaves the record's path out, any(A) under either keeps it record_verified

Q-motif.title: motif
Q-motif.prose: `predicate_scope` `motif` asks the predicate once of the pattern as a whole, on the union of the labels over all its contexts. A toy example, not an executed test: suppose a pattern has two contexts, one carrying label A alone and one carrying label B alone; `all(A, B)` at motif scope is true, since the union holds both, although no single context carries both and the same predicate at context scope would select neither. `decided_by` names the evidence the verdict rests on, never the quantifier of the predicate: `every_context` says that every raw context was tested, not that each satisfied the predicate; `tested_contexts` that a budget cut the pass; `no_instance` that the pattern has no context on this graph. The tests, in mode count on a 25 bp window of mge: `any(A)` gives `motif.selected` true with `decided_by` `every_context` and A among `labels_present` (`motif`); `none(A)` on the same window gives false, `every_context`; a random 31 bp pattern with no context gives false with `decided_by` `no_instance`, a verdict on the empty set: the pattern was not found, which is no evidence about the absence of any label (section 25.3, 25.6). The two option edges: `predicate_scope` motif without a predicate is refused (400 `invalid_request` naming `predicate_scope`, section 25.2), and `predicate_strands` without a predicate is a no-op the host accepts, the answer the one without it (`contains_source_context`: the source found). The latter is the chapter's split case: the service refuses an option that would act on nothing (`pattern.predicate_options_noop_without_predicate`), so via MCP that pair stands by design and the no-op is shown on the direct access paths only. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path it was exercised on.]] [[n_mcp_by_design ? Via MCP {n_mcp_by_design:word} pair{n_mcp_by_design:s} stand{n_mcp_by_design:v} by design ({mcp_refused_before_host_codes}; see B)[[!mcp_by_design_all_verified ?, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified} unverified]].]]
Q-motif.claim: the motif question is answered on the union of the labels over the pattern's contexts (decided_by naming the evidence read, not a per-context quantifier) or stated as no_instance, and motif without a predicate is refused

Q-budget.title: budgets
Q-budget.prose: The two selection budgets at 1 on a 25 bp window of cje, whose seven offsets in its own record already put the raw count above 1. `max_predicate_contexts` 1 in `all_or_count` does not admit the pass: the list is withheld as `predicate_above_threshold` with nothing read (`withheld`); in `partial` the raw release is cut at 1 and the first context tested (`cut` `max_predicate_contexts`); `max_predicate_work` 1 under `context` strands stops the pass after its first read, since the budget is checked before every read and a row costs at least 8 units (section 19.9: the first read passes the gate at 0 units spent, the second does not): `stop` with the phase selection and the reason `max_predicate_work` and the list withheld as `predicate_budget` (`stop`, `withheld`). The invariants check that each stated reason is one section 19.8 lists and can have happened (a `predicate_above_threshold` needs the raw count above the cap, a `predicate_budget` a predicate stop). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every access path: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every access path.]]
Q-budget.claim: a selection above max_predicate_contexts is not admitted or cut as the mode says, and max_predicate_work stops the pass with the stated stop

Q-pred-forms.property: Under predicate_strands context the record's contexts are selected exactly as the form says: any(A), at_least 1 of (A, human) and and(any A, not any human) select them with A at strand context or both; none(A), all(A, human) and at_least 2 of (A, human) leave them out of a complete filtered list (the negative forms assume, without proof, that the human column lacks the window).
Q-pred-forms.question: Are the record's own contexts selected exactly as each operator says under context strands, and left out of a complete filtered list where the form is false?

Q-pred-either.property: Under predicate_strands either the four simple forms select as they say: any(A) and all(A) select the record's contexts, none(A) and not(any A) leave them out.
Q-pred-either.question: Do the four simple forms select or leave out the record's contexts as they say under either strands?

Q-pred-unknown.property: An unknown label is listed in predicate.unknown_labels; any() of it folds to false (normal form false, selection.pass constant, selected exact 0, note predicate_constant), none() of it to true (every context selected).
Q-pred-unknown.question: Is an unknown label reported, and does any() of it fold to false and none() of it to true without reading a row?

Q-pred-refusals.property: A number as a name and predicate_only without a predicate are refused with 400 invalid_request and the host's exact text (the first names the fix); via MCP the service refuses both at submit, by design.
Q-pred-refusals.question: Are a number as a name and predicate_only without a predicate refused with the host's exact text?

Q-strands.property: any(A) under either on a 16S 20-mer the record holds on both strands: the + contexts selected by their own row (selection_strands context or both), at least one - context selected through its reverse complement's row (reverse_complement or both); the strand named is the row read, not a strand observation.
Q-strands.question: Under either strands, is a + context selected by its own row and at least one - context through its reverse complement's row, with the row named?

Q-more.property: The '-' source contexts of a reverse-complemented window are selected by their own rows under context strands; or() selects; at_least n outside 1 .. the list's length is refused with the path of the fault.
Q-more.question: Is a - source context selected by its own row under context strands, does or() select, and is at_least n outside the list's length refused?

Q-supported.property: Supported paths under none(A) in partial exclude the record's own path; under any(A) with either strands the record's path is listed record_verified with its occurrence at the window.
Q-supported.question: Does a predicate select among supported paths: none(A) leaving the record's own path out, any(A) under either keeping it record_verified?

Q-motif.property: predicate_scope motif: selected true / false is the predicate on the union of the contexts' labels, decided_by every_context naming that every raw context was read (not that each satisfied the predicate); no_instance on an absent pattern; motif without a predicate is refused, predicate_strands alone is a no-op the host answers (and the service refuses).
Q-motif.question: Is the motif verdict the predicate on the union of the contexts' labels, with decided_by naming the evidence, and is motif without a predicate refused?

Q-budget.property: max_predicate_contexts 1 is not admitted in all_or_count (withheld predicate_above_threshold) and cut in partial (cut max_predicate_contexts); max_predicate_work 1 stops the pass after its first read (stop selection / max_predicate_work, withheld predicate_budget).
Q-budget.question: Is a selection above max_predicate_contexts withheld or cut as the mode says, and does max_predicate_work stop the pass with the stated stop?
